_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never fetched by the student's browser until a teacher/marker PDF is generated. Never render any of this on the student-facing page. See CLAUDE.md section 5's assessment-security amendment.

markingScheme.criterion: Quotes the Spanish words of one real task from their own Record (e.g. 'fuimos', 'comió', 'Fue divertido') that they got wrong or needed two tries for.
markingScheme.accept: Any task that appears in the student's own Record with Tries 2 or Right = No; if the student had a perfect Record, any task from the Record. Accents not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: Describing a rule in general with no task or Spanish words taken from their Record.

markingScheme.criterion: States the correct rule behind that task in English (e.g. each person has its own past ending: -é/-í for yo, -aste/-iste for tú, -ó/-ió for él/ella, -amos/-imos for nosotros, -aron/-ieron for ellos; or fue can mean 'went' (from ir) or 'was' (from ser) and the rest of the sentence tells you which; or past-time words like ayer signal the past).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct rule that fits the quoted task, in the student's own words.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'I got it wrong' or 'it changes' with no stated reason or pattern.

markingScheme.criterion: Writes one new, correct Spanish example that follows the stated rule.
markingScheme.accept: Any grammatically correct past-tense example (minor accent slips allowed if the form is clear), different from the quoted task.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating the quoted task, or a new example with an incorrect verb form for the person.

markingScheme.criterion: Sentence 1 uses a correct preterite form of ir (fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fueron) to match the person, followed by a + a place, and includes a past-time word (ayer, anoche, el año pasado, la semana pasada...).
markingScheme.accept: Any correct form of ir matching the person plus a place and a past-time word. Minor accent slips are allowed.
markingScheme.insufficient: A present-tense form (voy), a wrong form for the person, no place, or no past-time word.

markingScheme.criterion: Sentence 2 uses a correct preterite form of comer (comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comieron) to match the person, with something that was eaten.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct form of comer matching the person plus a food or meal. Minor accent slips are allowed.
markingScheme.insufficient: Present tense (como), an -ar ending (comé), or no food stated.

markingScheme.criterion: Sentence 3 uses a correct preterite form of visitar (visité, visitaste, visitó, visitamos, visitaron) to match the person, with a place or thing visited.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct form of visitar matching the person plus a place. Minor accent slips are allowed.
markingScheme.insufficient: Present tense (visito), an -er/-ir ending (visitió), or no place stated.

criteria.source: = the Explain question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points achieved: no real task quoted from the Record, no correct rule, and no correct new example.
Achieves only ONE of the three: quotes a real task from their Record OR states a correct rule OR gives a correct new example — the other two are missing or incorrect.
Achieves TWO of the three: e.g. quotes a real task and states the correct rule, but the new example is missing or incorrect.
Quotes a real task from their own Record, states the correct rule in English, and gives a correct new Spanish example — all three analytic points present.

criteria.source: = the Apply question's 3-point marking scheme above, one-to-one. Do not award these marks a second time here.

levels.descriptor: None of the three analytic points achieved: ir sentence with place and past-time word, comer sentence, and visitar sentence are all missing or incorrect.
Achieves only ONE of the three analytic points (correct ir sentence with place and past-time word; correct comer sentence; correct visitar sentence).
Achieves TWO of the three analytic points.
Correct ir sentence with place and past-time word, correct comer sentence, and correct visitar sentence — all three analytic points present.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across BOTH the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks in use_of_evidence and spanish_use above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the meaning to be followed reliably.
Main meaning understandable, but organisation, vocabulary or precision cause some difficulty.
Clear and logical, uses Unit 8 vocabulary, and is easy to follow. Minor spelling or accent slips that do not harm meaning are not penalised.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply). Award marks point-by-point using each question's markingScheme: each point is worth the marks stated, is independent unless it names a dependsOn point (award it only if that earlier point was also awarded), and each point's 'accept'/'insufficient' tell you what does and doesn't count. use_of_evidence's 3 marks ARE the Explain markingScheme's 3 points, and spanish_use's 3 marks ARE the Apply markingScheme's 3 points — the rubric levels restate the same points as bands; award each set once, not twice. communication is a separate, holistic 2 marks across both answers. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy. Use the student's logged Record (nivel/tarea/respuesta/correcto/intentos in simulation_results.trials) to verify any task they claim to quote. Students are beginners (A1): accept valid alternative wording and do not penalise a missing accent (e.g. accept comi for comí). Total is out of 15 (7 auto + 3 + 3 + 2). Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
